posts.name: Mirasol
posts.cooked:
Dailyalice:

Has Blizzard ever made a statement about whether player actions and chat in game are being used to train LLMs or AIs outside of the game? (I’m not referring to the chatbots that monitor for dirty words.)

For WoW? No they have not said anything about that.

They have extensive connections with some of the early AI research efforts though such as the collaboration between Blizzard Starcraft II and Deep Mind. That was announced in 2016 at Blizzcon.

Google DeepMind

DeepMind and Blizzard to release StarCraft II as an AI research environment

Today at BlizzCon 2016 in Anaheim, California, we announced our collaboration with Blizzard Entertainment to open up StarCraft II to AI and Machine Learning researchers around the world.

In 2019 they did release some more info on progress.

news.blizzard.com

DeepMind Research on Ladder

Experimental versions of DeepMind’s StarCraft II agent, AlphaStar, will soon play a small number of games on the competitive ladder in Europe as part of ongoing research into AI.

Dailyalice:

I’m fairly certain Microsoft has the right to feed every word we type in game or speak in voice chat into an LLM trainer.

Blizzard does own our Battlenet accounts, characters, items, and everything we do or say on their platforms (Bnet chat, games, and forums). So technically you are right. They can do what they want with the game data provided PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION (PII) is protected as required by law. The real life information (name, address, phone number, email, financial info) can not be used in any way that is not detailed in the Privacy Policy and approved by the user.

Dailyalice:

(I’m not referring to the chatbots that monitor for dirty words.)

Surprisingly enough, they don’t have one yet. They have the crude filter that scrambles things based on the settings, but that is not a learning model. That is the same filter we have had since 2004 pretty much. Very simple list of things the game checks the chat against.

So while they don’t currently do that, they could. Of course, an LLM would not really get much useful out of game chat. Spam ads, trolling, some legit trade, and rare civil chat.

What would be useful for them, and I could see them doing, is monitoring gameplay behavior for anti-cheat purposes - maybe eventually an AI assistant to the Warden software? Warden works like antivirus in that they program in definitions of what they are looking for. I could also see them using gameplay and a learning model to help train a Follower AI for solo dungeons and content.

They have said nothing about any of that though. Blizz is not jumping on the AI bandwagon very fast.

posts.name: Llew
posts.cooked:
I understand it seems like that data, those chat logs, would be full of nonsense, but LLMs are getting so fast and sophisticated at making connections it’s unwise to think we can see in advance the kind of connections they will make. It’s hubris to think this stuff couldn’t be used to personally identify you; they have IP information, they have login names and passwords and e-mail addresses, those are all tied to your Bnet ID. It would be trivial for a human, let alone a LLM, to connect those dots.
Just because they’re not supposed to doesn’t mean the AIs won’t without permission.
